mx.teacher_note: Moon is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: On a full Moon day, the Moon is nearly opposite the Sun.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: the illuminated portion facing Earth changes -> the observed phase changes. happens first, and that produces Moon-Sun separation as seen from Earth changes.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when On a full Moon day, the Moon is nearly opposite the Sun is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: When the Moon is toward the Sun, little or none of its illuminated half faces Earth; when it is opposite the Sun, the illuminated half faces Earth as a full Moon. Moon-Sun separation as seen from Earth changes -> the illuminated portion facing Earth changes -> the observed phase changes. The learner correctly applies this rule: When the Moon is toward the Sun, little or none of its illuminated half faces Earth; when it is opposite the Sun, the illuminated half faces Earth as a full Moon. Full Moon just means a bright Moon at night, so the Moon's direction from the Sun does not matter.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: The night sky: Moon and calendars. The student must decide: Use the Moon's position relative to the Sun to decide whether the visible phase is new, full, waxing, or waning. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Supply exactly one complete tikzpicture.
